posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Play now on Steam!

Our yearly tradition is returning soon... 👀

Observing the early universe would be such a fascinating and relaxing experience... or would it be?

We imagine advanced alien civilizations building gigantic spaceships, Dyson spheres and empires spanning entire galaxies. But what if true technological progress goes in exactly the opposite direction? Not outward into space, but deeper and deeper into the smallest layers of reality?

What is the Barrow Scale? How powerful could a civilization become by mastering DNA, and even fundamental particles, and could the universe already be filled with godlike civilizations hiding in plain sight? Watch
Let's visit some of the most dangerous neighbourhoods... in space!

Our curiosity to learn more about the stars is endless. Today, some scientists pursue their passion by building large telescopes that are able to capture the faintest glimmer of stars billions of light-years away. Some telescopes are even launched from Earth to get a clearer view outside the atmosphere. But what about the opportunity to see the stars with your own eyes, unfiltered? Astronauts, like the one that can be seen on the September page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, say nothing compa

Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!

recentPosts.caption:
Some mornings in Cappadocia come with a little extra drama. 🦚⁠
@thepersianwonderer woke up to peacocks wandering through the beautiful surroundings of @museumhotel, with the landscapes of Uçhisar making the perfect backdrop.⁠
⁠
A pretty unforgettable way to start the day in Cappadocia.

A hidden sanctuary built right into the heart of the rock. ⛰️⁠
The Temple of Valadier, an elegant octagonal chapel tucked inside the Frasassi cave in Genga, Marche.⁠
Built in 1828 at the request of Pope Leo XII, the neoclassical chapel was created as a place for peace and spiritual reflection.⁠
⁠
What makes it so fascinating is the contrast between the perfectly symmetrical architecture and the raw, ancient rock surrounding it, a beautiful meeting point between human craftsmanship and nature. ⁠

These photos made our day!⁠
⁠
The photographer caught these adorable photos of this chipmunk right in the middle of a big stretch, and it looks like this little one was getting ready for whatever the day had in store.⁠
⁠
Which photo is your favorite? 😍⁠
⁠
By: @chiimo.co

This flower turns transparent when it rains. 🌧️⁠
⁠
Known as the skeleton flower, Diphylleia grayi, has petals with a loose, porous structure. When rain fills the tiny spaces between the plant cells, light passes through the petals more easily, making them appear almost completely transparent.⁠
⁠
As the petals dry, the air returns to those spaces and they become white again.⁠
⁠
By: @nora.n_kt52

When the mountains meet the sky, the view does all the talking. 🏔️☁️⁠
One of those incredible moments where endless mountain landscapes blend perfectly into the sky, creating a scene that almost doesn’t look real.⁠
⁠
The kind of nature you could stare at for hours. 🌿💙⁠
🎥: @mariarodion

This pink hotel is a brutalist dream. 💗⁠
⁠
Laiva Hotel in San José del Cabo, Mexico, combines bold concrete forms with soft pink and coral tones, creating a look that feels very different from the typical resort.⁠
⁠
Designed by Tasman, the boutique hotel features curved walls, private patios, a pool, and a rooftop overlooking the historic center of San José del Cabo.⁠
⁠
Would you book a stay here?⁠
⁠
By: @laiva.sanjose @be.tasman

Some traditions are best experienced with your ears. 🇰🇿🎶⁠
⁠
The Shankobyz is an ancient Kazakh mouth instrument traditionally associated with nomadic culture, producing soft, rhythmic vibrations that can sound almost hypnotic.⁠
Imagine sitting by a campfire, surrounded by endless steppe, with nothing but the wind and these unique melodies in the background. 🔥🌾⁠
⁠
A beautiful reminder that culture isn’t only something we see sometimes, it’s something we hear.⁠
🎥: @visitmekazakhstan

A beautiful reminder that every life matters. 🥹🐾🌿⁠
@terra_ronca_goias captured a touching moment in nature, where a wild animal in danger is given a helping hand.⁠
⁠
In moments like these, protecting wildlife is as simple as noticing when help is needed, and choosing to step in. 🤍⁠
⁠
A wholesome encounter that restores a little faith in humanity.⁠
🎥: @terra_ronca_goias

There's something so magical about Paris at night & photographer @raphaelmetivet captured it beautifully. ✨⁠
⁠
These photos show a quieter side of the city, with softly lit streets, historic buildings, and little corners that feel completely different after dark.⁠
⁠
But what’s even more special is that every window seems to tell a different story, with warm lights and glimpses of life inside.⁠
⁠
The last photo is our favorite! 😍 Which one is yours?

A forest that looks like it belongs in another world. 🌿💚⁠
Moss-covered walls, leaves dripping with rain, and the soft sound of water running through the trees, everything here feels alive and untouched.⁠
⁠
The kind of place where you naturally slow down, breathe deeper, and let nature do all the talking. 🌲✨⁠
🎥: @manuela_palmberger

Capilano Suspension Bridge Park really does feel like stepping into a fairytale, with towering trees, mossy forest trails, and the river running through the canyon.⁠
⁠
The famous suspension bridge stretches 137 meters across the canyon, while elevated walkways take you up into the rainforest canopy.⁠
⁠
Would you visit it?⁠
⁠
By: @princerphoto @bucketlistworldtravel

Dinner with an arrival you’ll never forget. 🌊🍽️⁠
The Rock Zanzibar, a restaurant sitting on a small rock in the Indian Ocean, just off the coast of Zanzibar.⁠
And getting there is part of the experience, depending on the tide, you can walk across the sand, wade through the water, or take a boat to the restaurant. 🚤✨⁠
⁠
So… which way would you want to arrive?⁠
🎥: @kescilyann
